fields.name: Agarilux
fields.description: An enormous purple mushroom. Its size and glowing protrusions make this fungus beautiful to look at. It dies when exposed to light.

fields.name: Agave
fields.description: A large-leafed desert plant with edible flowers and stalks.

fields.name: Alocasia
fields.description: A tropical plant. Its extremely broad leaves are a commonly-recognized signifier of tropical forests.

fields.name: Ambrosia bush
fields.description: A rare wild bush which yields the ambrosia fruit. Ambrosia fruit is delicious and produces a drug-like mood boost. Ambrosia cannot be farmed, which makes wild ambrosia groves very valuable.; Its rarity, beauty, and desirability are why ambrosia was named after the food of the ancient Greek gods.

fields.name: Anima grass
fields.description: A grass infused with luminous microorganisms. Tribal peoples find that anima grass grows around the base of an anima tree as they meditate. It seems to reflect some kind of strengthening of the tree's psychic power.; Offworld scientists have tried to study the phenomenon, but the grass degenerates into normal plant matter when observed too closely.; Animals refuse eat{Sic} anima grass. Tribal stories say this is done out of respect and fear.

fields.name: Anima tree
fields.description: A rare tree with warm, skin-smooth bark and long iridescent leaves. Infused with bioluminescent micro-organisms, anima trees develop a unique form of psychic symbiosis with surrounding lifeforms, allowing them to grow in a wide variety of biomes.; If a person (psycaster or not) meditates near an anima tree, it will grow anima grass around its base. Once enough grass is grown, it becomes possible to carry out a psychic linking ritual with the tree and upgrade a person's psychic powers. Only tribal peoples know the secret of this ritual. Tribal psycasters are also able to draw psyfocus from anima trees while meditating to them.; Anima trees' psychic properties are weakened if artificial structures are placed nearby. They refuse to be caged or studied, and must remain part of nature.; Most tribes believe that anima trees are not simply trees, but are rather the physical extremities of a single world spirit.

fields.name: Archean tree
fields.description: A tree bioengineered to terraform deadworlds and early-stage rimworlds. The tree hosts a special microbial community in its roots which enriches nearby terrain into rich soil. The trees are hardy enough to survive in the vacuum of space and produce a small amount of oxygen.; Archean trees are sterile, preventing them from becoming an invasive species after terraforming has been completed. They can only be grown from seeds produced on glitterworld planets. The tree's delicate root system prevents it from being replanted.

fields.name: Astragalus
fields.description: A small perennial wildflower that grows in alpine climates.

fields.name: Bamboo tree
fields.description: A fast-growing tree-like plant that grows in dense groves. Bamboo can be harvested for a wood-like material. The plant itself is not beautiful.

fields.name: Berry bush
fields.description: A bushy wild plant which yields delicious berries. Berries can be cooked, but they're also good to eat even when raw.

fields.name: Birch tree
fields.description: A temperate-biome tree known for its thin, white, paper-like bark.

fields.name: Bonsai tree
fields.description: A small tree, pruned and shaped to look visually pleasing.

fields.name: Boomshroom
fields.description: These mushrooms produce volatile chemicals as a defensive measure. They can be harvested for chemfuel. However, this must be done with extreme caution, as the mushrooms can explode if they're destroyed.; Glitterworld researchers have used genetic material from boomshrooms to bioengineer a number of chemfuel-producing animals.

fields.name: Brambles
fields.description: Tangled, thorny, woody shoots covered with leaves. Brambles grow in clusters, and slow down anyone moving over them.

fields.name: Bryolux
fields.description: A blue moss typically found in deep, dark caves. It is sticky, with tangled fibers, which slows anyone walking over it. Dies when exposed to light.

fields.name: Bulrush
fields.description: A plant commonly found in swamps, recognizable for its brown cigar-shaped top.

fields.name: Burned stump
fields.description: A burned tree stump. It's ugly and yields no usable wood.

fields.name: Bush
fields.description: A short shrub. Does not typically talk.

fields.name: Cecropia tree
fields.description: One of the most common rainforest trees. Cecropia grows very fast, but yields little usable wood.

fields.name: Chokevine
fields.description: Tangled masses of cord-like, spiky vines which coil in great masses along the ground. Chokevine greatly slows down anyone who moves over it. Multiple tribes have independently generated stories of chokevine strangling children to death in the night, as a way to scare kids into coming home before dark.

fields.name: Chopped stump
fields.description: A stump left behind after a tree has been felled. The stump can be extracted but yields very little usable wood. Left outdoors, the stump will deteriorate in time.

fields.name: Clivia
fields.description: An unusual plant with tall, pretty flowers. Some call it the 'bush lily'.

fields.name: Cocoa tree
fields.description: A tropical tree that produces chocolate, genetically engineered to sweeten its own product, and survive in slightly less-warm climates.

title: Corn plant

fields.name: Corn plant
fields.description: A tall grain plant which produces ears of soft, edible seeds. While corn takes a long time to grow, it yields lots of food compared to other crops. Harvested corn takes a long time to spoil.

intro: The corn plant has a long growing cycle and a very high yield of 22 pieces of corn. It cannot be sown in hydroponics. Corn plants have a base growing time of 11.3 days, need a minimum soil fertility of 70%, and have a fertility sensitivity rating of 100%. Corn has the second-highest base yield per day (approx. 2.7% less than rice), but requires the least farming labor to maintain due to its long g

fields.name: Cotton plant
fields.description: A mid-size crop that yields fine white cotton fibers. These are used to make cloth.

fields.name: Cypress tree
fields.description: A tall coniferous tree often found in swamps. Despite its slow growth, planting these trees can be profitable as a low-effort, long-term investment because they yield so much usable wood.

title: Dandelions

fields.name: Dandelions
fields.description: A tiny yellow flower which grows in large clusters. Though it is often considered a weed, dandelions in bloom are quite beautiful.

intro: Dandelions are a common beautiful flower that can be sown but also grows naturally in .

title: Daylily

fields.name: Daylily
fields.description: A cultivated flower with wide petals and a short lifespan. Daylilies are very beautiful, but must be replanted often.

intro: Daylilies are a decorative plant that have relatively high beauty, but need to be replanted often. They can be grown indoors, simply using the light from a torch or standing lamp.

fields.name: Devilstrand mushroom
fields.description: This fragile mushroom was genetically engineered to produce a silk net that is both difficult to tear and soft to the touch. While the mushroom takes a very long time to grow, only exotic ultra-tech fabrics outperform its devilstrand fibers.; Some say it's called devilstrand because of its red color. Others think it owes its name to the greed it inspires in people.

fields.name: Drago tree
fields.description: A hardy desert tree topped with thick, pointed leaves.

fields.name: Fibercorn
fields.description: An inedible, fibrous plant which produces a small amount of a wood-like substance.

fields.name: Fireweed
fields.description: A low-lying plant that produces clusters of purple flowers. It is common in alpine environments.

fields.name: Gauranlen moss
fields.description: Symbiotic moss that grows near Gauranlen trees.

fields.name: Gauranlen pod
fields.description: A small pod that protects a single Gauranlen seed. This seed can be harvested and used to plant a Gauranlen tree.

fields.name: Gauranlen tree
fields.description: A large, distinctive-looking tree with a unique life-cycle. Each Gauranlen tree contains a small non-conscious dryad queen. The queen births creatures called dryads which guard and tend the tree. In exchange, the tree nurtures its protectors by feeding them directly. From the outside, it appears the dryads are created by the tree directly and act as part of it.; It is possible for a person to form a connection with a Gauranlen tree and partially control the dryads it produces.; Some say Gauranlen trees are the homes of nature spirits that follow humanity across worlds.

fields.name: Giant rafflesia
fields.description: A rare, giant flower which can be found deep in steaming jungles. You would think a giant flower would be beautiful, but this one looks and smells like rotting flesh.

fields.name: Glowstool
fields.description: A small brown mushroom typically found in caves. It smells like an old, dirty rag pulled from the stomach of a rotting muffalo - but it tastes surprisingly good when cooked. Dies when exposed to light.

fields.name: Grass
fields.description: Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.

fields.name: Gray grass
fields.description: Gray grass refers to a variety of species of wild toxin-adapted grass. It grows anywhere there is minimally-fertile polluted ground and the climate isn't overwhelming hostile.

fields.name: Gray pine tree
fields.description: A small toxin-adapted tree with twisted branches. It can only grow on polluted terrain, and yields a meager amount of wood when harvested.

fields.name: Harbinger tree
fields.description: A gnarled tree that grows a flesh-like covering around a bioferrite skeleton. Harbinger trees are capable of feeding on corpses and raw meat, and will consume those placed nearby. If well fed, the grove will continue to grow.; The tree can be harvested for twisted meat and bioferrite.; In a tribal myth, these trees are the emissaries of a mad, shapeless god who rules an endless black ocean. The myth ends after the shapeless god reaches up from the water and tears down the sky.

title: Haygrass

fields.name: Haygrass
fields.description: A mixture of nutrient-rich grasses which yield large amounts of hay. Hay is edible for animals, but not humans.

intro: Haygrass has a base growing time of 7 days, needs a minimum soil fertility of 70%, and has a fertility sensitivity rating of 60%. The following table details how long it takes for haygrass to grow in each growable ground type, factoring in the plant resting time and being in ideal growing conditions:

title: Healroot

fields.name: Healroot
fields.description: A slow-growing plant which yields herbal medicine when harvested. Sowing and harvesting healroot are both very labor-intensive tasks because of its delicate shoots.; Healroot was selectively bred for centuries by settlers. It is sometimes also called "healer's hand" by tribespeople - a nickname it owes to its five major medicinal virtues.

intro: }} Sowing healroot requires a minimum growing skill of , but any colonist capable of plant cutting can harvest them.

title: Hop plant

fields.name: Hop plant
fields.description: A flowering crop that yields hops, an essential ingredient in beer.

intro: Sowing hop plants requires a minimum growing skill of , but any colonist capable of plant cutting can harvest them.

fields.name: Lily pad
fields.description: A water plant with a broad floating leaf.

fields.name: Lotus
fields.description: An aquatic plant known for its fragrant flowers.

fields.name: Low shrubs
fields.description: Various low broadleaf shrubs. These grow in clusters and slow down movement.

fields.name: Magma cactus
fields.description: A resilient species of cactus notable for its ability to survive extreme heat.

fields.name: Maple tree
fields.description: A common medium-sized tree, easily identifiable by its distinct three-pointed leaf.

fields.name: Moss
fields.description: Wild moss that grows in clumps in areas of low light and cool temperatures. Moss takes a long time to grow, but is very frost-resistant.

fields.name: Night grass
fields.description: A grass-like fungus that grows as part of a massive mycelium network.

fields.name: Night rafflesia
fields.description: A distant cousin of the giant rafflesia, this plant has adapted to thrive in dark locations. Its beauty is tempered by a strong stench of musk and rotten eggs.

fields.name: Nutrifungus
fields.description: A meaty bioengineered mushroom grown for its nutritious value. It can grow on fungal gravel, but only in darkness - exposing it to any kind of light, including darklights, will kill it.

fields.name: Oak tree
fields.description: A hardwood tree. Oaks take a long time to grow, but their wood is so strong that 'oak' is used as a metaphor for strength across many cultures.

fields.name: Palm tree
fields.description: A tropical tree with a tall, naked trunk topped by a cluster of very broad leaves. Unfortunately, this variety doesn't produce any edible coconuts.

fields.name: Pebble cactus
fields.description: A small cactus that resembles a cluster of pebbles. It can only grow on polluted terrain. It yields a meager amount of woody fiber when harvested.

fields.name: Pincushion cactus
fields.description: A short cactus. It is so named because it resembles a pincushion.

fields.name: Pine tree
fields.description: A large conifer covered with prickly pine cones. It grows in a distinctive conical shape.

fields.name: Polux tree
fields.description: After generations of exposure, these trees have evolved to metabolize pollutants. By drawing pollutants from the ground through wide root networks, they slowly clean polluted terrain in their vicinity. However, they cannot do this if buildings are constructed over their roots.; Unlike most methods of cleaning polluted terrain, polux trees do not create toxic wastepacks.

fields.name: Poplar tree
fields.description: A softwood tree that grows very fast. Unfortunately, its wood is weak and so it yields less useful material than hardwood trees.

fields.name: Potato plant
fields.description: A highly nutritious tuber. Potatoes grow well even in somewhat poor soil, and form a delicious crispy outer coating when fried in oil.

fields.name: Psilocap
fields.description: A fungus that gives off hallucinogenic spores. Standing next to them is enough to produce mild hallucinations. Psilocaps can be harvested and ingested to produce a vivid sensory experience that increases the user's mood.

title: Psychoid plant

fields.name: Psychoid plant
fields.description: A leafy plant which generates the chemical compound psychite. Originally evolved as a defense mechanism to ward off plant-eating animals by overstimulating and sickening them, the psychite drug can be extracted and refined into various forms for recreational use. It is addictive.

intro: }} Sowing psychoid plants requires a minimum growing skill of , but any colonist capable of plant cutting can harvest them. Psychoid plants are one of the few plants that can be planted and grown on polluted tiles.

fields.name: Rat palm tree
fields.description: A tree similar to a palm tree with dense surface roots. It can only grow on polluted terrain. When harvested, it yields a meager amount of wood.

fields.name: Reeds
fields.description: A tall slender plant that grows in water.

title: Rice plant

fields.name: Rice plant
fields.description: A short, fast-growing crop that yields small edible grains. Its great nutritional output and ease of cultivation has made it the economic core of many great civilizations. While rice grows quickly, it is sensitive to soil fertility and will not fare well in poor soil.

intro: Rice plants yield rice, a fast growing crop. While its speed nets a high overall yield per tile per day, each plant gives the least food per harvest, so rice takes a high amount of labor for a given amount of food. Therefore, it is a good option for newer colonies, but may be gradually phased out as a food reserve is established.

fields.name: Ripthorn
fields.description: A short toxin-adapted shrub that looks like a dense, tough tangle of thorny branches. Difficult to move through, it slows down anyone moving over it. It can only grow in polluted areas.

title: Rose

fields.name: Rose
fields.description: A beautiful cultivated flower, the rose has been a symbol of love since Earth's ancient era.

intro: Roses can be sown by Growers in plant pots or in Growing zone. Sowing requires {{Ticks|}} of work.

fields.name: Saguaro cactus
fields.description: A large cactus native to arid Earth environments. Though it is not a tree, it yields a small amount of fibrous material that can be used like wood.

fields.name: Smashed stump
fields.description: The remnants of a tree destroyed by damage. It's ugly. The stump can be extracted but yields very little usable wood. Left outdoors, the stump will deteriorate in time.

fields.name: Smokeleaf plant
fields.description: A leafy crop grown for the psychological effects of chemicals in its leaves. Smokeleaf leaves can be prepared into joints at the crafting spot. Smokeleaf makes a user feel relaxed, but reduces motivation, and can be addictive.

fields.name: Snagroot tree
fields.description: A gnarled slow-growing tree, adapted to live in toxic scarlands. When harvested, it yields a meager amount of wood.

fields.name: Strawberry plant
fields.description: A low bush-like plant that yields fragile but delicious strawberries. While it isn't quite as productive calorie-for-calorie as other crops, strawberries are delicious even when raw.

fields.name: Tall grass
fields.description: Wild tall grass. Slows down anyone moving over it.

fields.name: Tall yellow grass
fields.description: Wild tall grass that grows in tough thickets. It slows down anyone moving over it.

fields.name: Teak tree
fields.description: An exceptionally strong hardwood tree that grows in warm climates. Because teak wood is so durable and water-resistant, it was used to form the keel of wooden sailing ships in ancient times.

fields.name: Thornvine
fields.description: A prickly vine adapted to living in harsh conditions.

fields.name: Timbershroom
fields.description: A tall brown mushroom with a long stem. When harvested, it yields a wood-like substance.

fields.name: Tinctoria
fields.description: A genetically-engineered flower-like crop which secretes a self-altering dye. Tinctoria dye can be coaxed into different colors and used to dye apparel.

fields.name: Toxipotato plant
fields.description: A genetically-engineered variant of potato adapted for growing in polluted areas. Compared to regular potatoes, toxipotatoes take less time to grow but yield a meager harvest of food. When eaten raw, they have a high chance of causing food poisoning. In spite of this, they have saved many settlers from starvation after toxic events.

fields.name: Wild healroot
fields.description: A slow-growing plant which yields herbal medicine when harvested.; This wild breed of healroot is hardier than domesticated healroot, but too difficult to cultivate. It is prized by tribespeople in colder climates.

fields.name: Willow tree
fields.description: One of the fastest growing shade trees, willows provide a beautiful, leafy canopy. It doesn't yield much usable wood.

fields.name: Willowgill
fields.description: A tall spindly slow-growing mushroom with gills that droop like a willow tree. It gives off a soft light.

fields.name: Witchwood tree
fields.description: A small toxin-adapted tree with a twisted trunk. It can only grow on polluted terrain. When harvested, it yields a meager amount of wood.

fields.name: Yellow grass
fields.description: Wild grass. Grows anywhere there is a little light and minimally fertile ground.
